channel.title: Boxy Trucks Field Notes
channel.description: 4x4 news, with an opinion, from BoxyTrucks.

item.title: Scout is welding real trucks in South Carolina. I love that. Your wait is still 2028.
item.description: Scout has started building Traveler and Terra validation vehicles at its $2 billion plant in Blythewood, South Carolina. None will be sold. Production is still 2027, deliveries still 2028, and 87% of reservation holders want the gas range extender.

item.title: The Patrol name is back in America. It's a sticker, but the truck under it is real.
item.description: For 2027 the Armada PRO-4X becomes the Armada Patrol PRO-4X, the first Patrol badge sold in the US since 1969. The hardware hasn't changed, and that's the most useful thing to know if you're shopping.

item.title: Three old trucks, 2,000 miles, one breakdown. This is the whole point.
item.description: Filmmaker Sam Newton and friends took two 60 Series Land Cruisers and an early Bronco on a 10-day, 2,000-mile run through the Southwest. One had transmission trouble before they left LA. Watch it, then read what to check before you buy your own.

item.title: Jeep just put independent front suspension on a Wrangler. Don’t panic.
item.description: The Wrangler Scrambler SRT concept is the first Wrangler ever without a solid front axle. It’s a desert runner, not a Rubicon replacement, and here’s what that means if you’re shopping.
